cases.doc: `exec_op` was called with no plan armed. Only a pool, during a flash loan\nwhose plan this receiver's owner armed, may trigger execution.
cases.name: NotArmed

cases.doc: The `caller` Blend passed to `exec_op` is not the armed initiator.
cases.name: BadCaller

cases.doc: After running the plan we hold less than the loan plus fee, so the\ninitiator's repayment would fail. Failing here gives a clear reason\ninstead of a generic pool error.
cases.name: InsufficientRepay

cases.doc: A plan with no steps is almost certainly a bot bug.
cases.name: EmptyPlan

cases.doc: A swap step's input token has zero balance here.
cases.name: NoInputBalance

udt_struct_v0.doc: An Aqua chained swap. `hops` are `(sorted_token_pair, pool_index, token_out)`\nexactly as `swap_chained` expects; the bot builds them from its quotes.
udt_struct_v0.name: AquaSwap

udt_struct_v0.doc: A Soroswap multi-hop swap. `amount_in == 0` means "everything we hold of\n`path[0]`", which is how a second step consumes the first step's output\nwithout the planner having to predict it exactly.
udt_struct_v0.name: SoroswapSwap

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A plan armed on a receiver, waiting for the pool's `exec_op` callback.

`initiator` is the `from` of the flash loan -- the address Blend will pass as
`caller` and the address the receiver hands the funds back to. Recorded at
arming time by the receiver's owner, because Soroban gives a callee no way to
learn who invoked it.

Lives in *temporary* storage for the duration of one transaction: written by
`set_plan`, consumed by `exec_op`. Soroban executes a transaction
sequentially, so nothing can observe or race it in between.
udt_struct_v0.name: Plan

udt_struct_v0.doc: Mirror of Blend's `Request`, declared here so it appears in this contract's\nown spec. The SDK's type is `export = false`, which leaves clients unable to\nencode arguments for `flash_execute`. Same fields, same wire encoding.
udt_struct_v0.name: Request

function_v0.doc:
Blend's flash-loan callback (`moderc3156::FlashLoan`). Called by the pool
after it has transferred the loan here and before it settles requests.

Runs the armed plan, then hands *everything* we hold of `token` back to
`caller`, whose `Repay` request the pool collects next. Anything above the
loan is profit and lands with the initiator too.
function_v0.name: exec_op

function_v0.doc:
Run a plan against funds this contract already holds. Owner only.

Cross-venue arbitrage without a flash loan, and the unwind path for a
liquidation position.
function_v0.name: execute

function_v0.doc:
Arm the plan that the next `exec_op` will run, and record who the loan's
`from` will be. Owner only, single-use.

Callable by an initiator contract (owner == initiator, in one
transaction) or by a wallet that owns this receiver directly and starts
the flash loan itself in a following transaction -- Blend's canonical
pattern, at the cost of a second ledger.
function_v0.name: set_plan

function_v0.doc: `owner` is the only address that can arm a plan, start a flash loan, run\na plan from held funds, or withdraw.
function_v0.name: __constructor

function_v0.doc:
Borrow `amount` of `asset` from `pool`, have `receiver` run `steps` with
it, then let the pool settle `requests` against us. Owner only.

For a pure arbitrage, `requests` is a single `Repay` of `amount` plus a
hair (dToken rounding at non-unit rates; Blend caps repayment at the
outstanding debt, so over-asking is safe). For a liquidation it is the
auction fill plus repayment of the liquidated debt, and we exit holding a
healthy position to unwind later.

Returns the change in our `asset` balance: realised profit.
function_v0.name: flash_execute
